newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Israel to meet on peace accord.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel to meet on peace accord.

text.p: Palestinian and Israeli officials overseeing implementation of PLO-Israel peace deals will meet on Monday for the first time since Israeli elections last May, a PLO official said on Sunday.
Saeb Erekat, head of the Palestinian side in the joint steering and monitoring committee, said Palestinians would focus on the issue of Hebron.

"Our priority in Monday's meeting is Hebron. We will discuss mechanisms for redeployment from Hebron after finalising protocols on deployment of temporary international presence in the city and joint patrols," Erekat told Reuters.
He said the meeting would take place at his West Bank office in PLO-ruled Jericho. Israeli officials could not be reached for comment.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat decided on the date during their first meeting last week which PLO officials and foreign diplomats said had revived stalled peace talks between the two sides.
Netanyahu had previously opposed the talks launched in 1993 by Israel's former Labour government.

Palestinians have complained that Netanyahu's government, formed in June, is not honouring the agreements -- foremost Israel's commitment to withdraw from the West Bank town of Hebron, home to 100,000 Palestinians and around 400 Jewish settlers.

Israel evacuated six West Bank cities and nearby villages under its interim accord with the PLO but delayed its withdrawal from Hebron after Islamic suicide bombings killed 59 people in the Jewish state in February and March.
Netanyahu has said he is examining ways to implement the withdrawal while guaranteeing the settlers' security.
A further Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank was scheduled to begin on September 7.

"We must also work on restoring confidence to dates. Israel yesterday made another violation to the agreements by missing the...date for starting redeployment from other parts of the West Bank," Erekat said.
He said Palestinians would ask Israel at the meeting to lift the closure imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip after the wave of bombings.
